root_motivation: On 2026-09-15 the burst lane's ccx53 prove failed checkcompat_ac02_ac03's broken-previous-binary test (exit Some(0), not 4) though the same commit passed on ccx43 minutes earlier. Cause: free_loopback_port bound then dropped a port before the child re-bound it; a parallel test's own server could grab that exact port in the gap, so /bin/false read as 'up'. More cores meant more concurrent test threads meant a higher collision rate -- a flaky mcphost test costs a box-hour and blocks enable on every image refresh. Separately, the 2026-09-16 redeploy of 0.54.1 logged compat_check=fail with its reason discarded: check-compat names the failing step on stderr, but mcphost-deploy's cli.py printed only the bare verdict (requirement 7 / AC9-AC10).
user_persona: Four (PRD User stories): (1) the burst lane on a 32-core box needs check-compat to pass for the same reason it passes on 16; (2) mcphost-deploy still gets exit 4 and the step name on a real failure, plus a redeploy log line naming which step, not just a bare verdict; (3) a test author spawning /bin/false needs no other test's server able to answer for it; (4) the operator sees the child's pid and matched token in the log on success.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a previous binary of /bin/false, When check_compat runs, Then it returns exit 4 naming step 'previous-up' within 1s and the log records the child's exit status.
Given a foreign HTTP server already answering 200 on the port check-compat chose, When wait_ready polls, Then it does not report ready and the log contains 'foreign server on port'.
Given a real previous mcphost binary, When it is spawned with the inherited listener and the token env, Then /healthz carries X-Mcphost-Compat-Token matching and check_compat reports ready.
Given MCPHOST_COMPAT_TOKEN unset, When /healthz is requested, Then no X-Mcphost-Compat-Token header is present.

Given cargo test -- --test-threads=32 running the two ac02/ac03 tests and 30 dummy tests that each spawn a real mcphost on a fresh listener, When the suite runs 200 times in a loop on RedBaron, Then 0 failures.
Given MCPHOST_BIND=127.0.0.1:<explicit port>, When check_compat runs against a real previous binary, Then it binds by address (log says so) and still enforces the token.
Given the whole mcphost test suite, When cargo test --workspace runs on RedBaron, Then it exits 0 and clippy is unchanged versus the committed baseline (delta-pass convention).
Given a real ccx53 burst box, When burst-lane.sh prove runs on this PRD's HEAD, Then prove done routed=true and the run log shows the ac02/ac03 tests ok.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did checkcompat_ac02_ac03's broken-previous-binary test read /bin/false as 'up'?
five_whys_trace.a: wait_ready polled a port a different, real mcphost test instance had grabbed in the gap between free_loopback_port() dropping its own listener and the /bin/false child (which never binds anything) being expected to bind it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why was there a gap between choosing the port and something actually holding it?
five_whys_trace.a: free_loopback_port() bound 127.0.0.1:0 purely to learn a free port number, then dropped the listener immediately, trusting the child to re-bind that exact number before anyone else could.

five_whys_trace.q: Why trust a re-bind instead of just keeping the first bind?
five_whys_trace.a: The previous release binds its own socket from $MCPHOST_BIND; there was no mechanism for check-compat to bind the socket itself and still let a separate previous-release process serve on it -- that mechanism (fd inheritance) didn't exist in mcphost's serve path yet.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does more concurrency make the race worse specifically for this test?
five_whys_trace.a: More test threads means more concurrently-running TestServer instances each doing their own bind-then-serve on ephemeral ports, raising the odds that some other real server's port exactly matches the port check-compat's /bin/false case just freed.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did a real schema-breaking compat failure and this race look identical after the fact?
five_whys_trace.a: mcphost migrate --check-compat always named the failing step on stderr, but mcphost-deploy's cli.py only ever printed the bare verdict (compat_check: fail) and journaled nothing beyond it, so the 2026-09-16 redeploy's real (or possibly race-caused) failure left no way to tell which it was after the fact -- requirement 7/AC9/AC10 fix the discarded reason, independent of the port-race fix itself.

ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Fixed in place, same 'amend the paper trail without reopening the contract' pattern used for every prior recurrence: no reviewer block yet, but the same staleness would recur if left byte-for-byte. root_motivation/user_persona/scope/non_goals/hard_constraints.additional/five_whys_trace were rewritten from this PRD's own Problem statement, Requirements, Non-goals, and Technical considerations sections; acceptance_criteria's ten entries point at the real tests/mcphost_data_retention_ac0[1-9,10]_*.rs files (AC1-6 exist, compile, and pass; AC7 is 'deferred' with no test file, matching the PRD's own AC7 wording that its proof is a live trailer read, not a build-time test; AC8-10 exist, compile, and pass); agent/test-map.json's ac_test_map was repointed to a new `retention` prefix and the prior `wasmkind` mapping preserved under ac_test_map_by_prefix (already present) rather than deleted. On the two build-time decisions: (1) `calls_resource_usage` is tracked in `retention_policy` (its own env-configurable window, `MCPHOST_RETENTION_CALLS_RESOURCE_USAGE_DAYS`, listed in host.usage/admin.usage the same as every other table) but has no entry in `retention::EXECUTABLE_TABLES` -- pruning `calls` by the `calls` window already deletes those same rows' `cpu_ms`/`peak_rss_kb` columns, so there is nothing left to independently delete under a second name; this is recorded in `PolicyTable`'s own doc comment, not silently dropped. (2) AC7 is listed as MUST (matching the PRD's own P0 marking) but deferred with no test, consistent with how this card's history already treats a PRD's own explicitly-live AC (see the share-a-tool-not-a-key entry above for AC6's identical shape) -- the coder dispatch instructions' own acceptance list confirms this by asking only for it to be named under `deferred` with a one-line reason, not built a mock for.

ambiguities_resolved.question: This card is now regenerated for PRD-mcphost-tenant-data-export, an entirely different feature (a tenant data-export job) from PRD-mcphost-data-retention (per-table retention pruning) that previously occupied it -- root_motivation, acceptance_criteria, scope, non_goals, user_persona, five_whys_trace, and hard_constraints.additional all needed a full rewrite, the same staleness class caught by reviewer-agent at least ten times in this card's own history (see the entries above) if left byte-for-byte. This PRD also carries its own Open Questions table with one entry due 'at build', owner Joe: 'Archive size cap per plan (assumed: free 50 MB, pro 1 GB)'. Two further ambiguities needed a build-time decision with no PRD text to settle them directly: (1) the technical considerations name 'the tenant's scratch quota' and 'the existing session-key material' for the signed URL, but neither concept exists anywhere in this codebase (`tenant_state.rs` has only a KV byte quota, and there is no prior signed-URL/session-key secret at all); (2) `runs.rs`'s executor only ever dispatches a `queued` run through a tenant's published `Kind`, but an export has no `Kind` to dispatch through.
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Fixed in place, same 'amend the paper trail without reopening the contract' pattern used for every prior recurrence: no reviewer block yet, but the same staleness would recur if left byte-for-byte. root_motivation/scope/non_goals/user_persona/five_whys_trace/hard_constraints.additional were rewritten from this PRD's own Problem statement, Goals, Non-goals, User stories, and Technical considerations sections; acceptance_criteria's seven entries point at the real tests/mcphost_tenant_data_export_ac0[1-3,5-7]_*.rs files (AC4 is Live, deferred, same convention as prior PRDs' own Live ACs -- see the share-a-tool-not-a-key entry above), with levels taken verbatim from the PRD's own P0/P1/P2 groupings (P0 -> MUST, P1/P2 -> SHOULD, no MUST-level regression risk since none of P1/P2 here guard an existing behavior). agent/test-map.json's ac_test_map was repointed to a new `tenantdataexport` prefix and the prior `retention` mapping preserved under ac_test_map_by_prefix (already present) rather than deleted. On the three build-time decisions: the size-cap open question shipped as `Plan.export_bytes_max` with exactly the PRD's own assumed numbers (free 50 MiB, pro 1 GiB), tolerant-defaulted for a `plans.toml` predating the key, same convention as every other per-plan quota in that file. 'The tenant's scratch quota' was realized as that same new plan-level byte cap (checked against the built archive) rather than inventing a new storage primitive, with the archive itself written under the host's existing data dir (`Db::data_dir()`) since no per-tenant scratch filesystem exists to reuse. 'The existing session-key material' was resolved as each tenant's own `key_hash` column -- already stored server-side, unique per tenant, unguessable (SHA-256 of a 32-byte random key) -- keying the same from-scratch `billing::hmac_sha256` this crate already has, so the URL's HMAC needs no new secret. The dispatch-through-a-Kind gap was resolved by never enqueuing an export as `queued` at all: `Db::start_export_run` inserts it straight into `running` (atomically checking for an already-running export first, for AC3), invisible to `runs::tick`'s leasing loop by construction, with `export::run_export_job` the only thing that ever finalizes it.

Additionally: (1) requirement 1's open question (does the production unit already socket-activate?) needed a real answer before choosing between its two branches; (2) AC1's required step name 'previous-up' differs from the pre-existing checkcompat_ac02_ac03.rs test's asserted 'spawn', while the PRD's technical considerations say not to edit that file 'beyond replacing the helper it calls'; (3) requirement 7/AC9/AC10 name a cross-repo edit (mcphost-deploy) that was already implemented and committed (edff67f7) by the time this coder session started, apparently by a concurrent build.
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: root_motivation/user_persona/scope/non_goals/hard_constraints.additional/five_whys_trace rewritten from this PRD's own Problem statement, User stories, Requirements, Non-goals, and Technical considerations sections; acceptance_criteria's test fields point at the real tests/checkcompat_race_ac0[1-7]_*.rs files (all exist, compile, and pass), AC8 marked deferred (no reachable burst box/burst-lane.sh in this sandbox), and AC9/AC10 point at the already-passing mcphost-deploy test files by absolute path rather than a tests/**/*.rs pointer, since requirement 7 is a Python change in a different repository. On the three ambiguities: (1) grep of src/main.rs/src/http.rs before this PRD's diff showed serve() only ever bound by address (deploy/*.service has no matching unit file in this repo either) -- so requirement 1 took its 'production does not already socket-activate; this PRD adds that support' branch, confirmed by the new inherited_listener()/serve_configured() pair in src/http.rs. (2) checkcompat_ac02_ac03.rs's one required edit is exactly the step-name string ('spawn' -> 'previous-up'), nothing else in that file changed, matching 'replacing the helper it calls' as narrowly as the AC1 requirement allows. (3) mcphost-deploy's commit edff67f7 (tests/checkcompatrace_ac9_journal_and_line_name_the_step.py, tests/checkcompatrace_ac10_ledger_scraper_reads_verdict.py) was inspected and re-run in this session (6 passed, 2 skipped -- skips gated on a real mcphost release binary this sandbox doesn't have -- 1 unrelated pre-existing failure elsewhere in that repo's suite, readymargin_ac3, predates this PRD by several commits) rather than redone.
